items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I call him Boot-whip so much, I can never think of his name. Anyhow, everybody knows who the other writer was.

ctx.x: Basie needed – he needed an alto [saxophone] player. We were in the Strand at the same time. The band was at its lowest ebb, so I got to thinking about my old buddies back home. I said, “Yeah. I got an alto player for you.” Ernie never played alto, but he was a great tenor [saxophone] player. I called him out of Basie’s dressing room while Basie was taking a steam shower, and of course the steam, “pssssssssss.” [He] couldn’t hear what I was saying, so I called Ernie, and I said, “Hey, man. You want to come join…
Did – was Joe Williams working with the band – with the small group too at the Brass Rail? Was he doing things in Chicago?
